comment: Prompt templates for card art (issue #49), after the style guide's prompt structure (docs/design/bird-collection/style-guide.md, 'Art direction'): the place's palette, the bird's anatomy and markings kept, subtle light, no typography, borders or logos. Since version 7 the model is FLUX.3 Image Klein (ADR-0007), which reads a full caption of the finished picture rather than an instruction, and addresses its references as <ref_image_0>, <ref_image_1>. Every painting takes the bird from <ref_image_0>: for pack and scene art the reference bird isolated on white (`isolate`, packbuilder.art), for photo art the birder's photo itself; scene art takes the place from <ref_image_1>, a telephoto crop of the glasses photo. Fields: {edition_light}, {edition_colors}, {edition_motifs}, {light}; {common_name} and {scientific_name} are available but unused, because a name pulls in the model's stereotype of the species and the reference is the identity. Pack art uses the edition's motifs; scene and photo art only its light and colours, as accents on the place's own colours, because a motif would be a claim about a place the photo does not show, and version 6's palette painted every house wall terracotta. FLUX.3's distilled model runs without guidance, so there is no negative prompt. History: Version 2 (the bake-off's second to fourth rounds, DECISIONS.md): scene and photo art no longer name the species, because a name pulls in the model's idea of the species (a red finch became a Northern Cardinal, a female or young bird a bright male), and the Legendary light keeps the bird's true colours. Version 3: scene art paints edge to edge, because version 2 sometimes ended in a ragged white paper edge. Version 4 (the maintainer's wording, 2026-10-14): an epic fantasy adventure-cover look in richly layered opaque gouache, with the bird kept entirely natural, after version 3 painted too tamely. Version 5: scene art paints a composite (packbuilder.art.paste_bird pastes the reference bird into the zoomed glasses photo), so its template keeps the pasted bird where it is instead of adding one from image 2; and a negative prompt, which counts now that the workflows run at full quality (cfg 4). Version 6: scene art takes the photo-art wording (keep the photographed moment), because at full quality the 'wilderness encounter' wording replaced a sharp glasses scene with an invented fantasy valley while this one kept it. Version 7: FLUX.3 Image Klein, a natural-history watercolour with touches of gouache, the bird from a reference on white (the maintainer's pick, 2026-10-19). The editions' themes live here until the packs' set definitions carry them (#54, #57). Bump the version when a template, an edition or a light changes.

light.standard: A few quiet gold flecks drift in the air.
light.legendary: It is a rare, legendary encounter: a luminous golden glow rises behind the bird, a warm rim of light traces its outline, the corners of the picture fall into deeper, atmospheric shadow, and fine flecks of gold leaf drift through the air. The bird itself keeps its true colours.

templates.pack: A hand-painted natural-history illustration in transparent watercolour with touches of gouache on warm cold-press paper, filling the picture edge to edge. The bird from <ref_image_0>, exactly as it appears there: the same pose and angle, the same feather pattern, colours and markings, the same bill, eye, legs and proportions, and the same sex and age (a dull female or young bird stays dull), nothing added and nothing taken away. Only the bird comes from <ref_image_0>, none of the branches, leaves, wires or background around it. It perches naturally in the middle of the picture, large in the frame, about half of its height, framed by {edition_motifs} painted loosely in soft washes, under {edition_light}, in {edition_colors} on a pale paper ground. The bird is painted in fine, confident detail with strokes that follow its feather tracts, crisp at the eye and bill, its colours true to <ref_image_0>; nothing covers its eye, bill or wing tips. {light} Visible paper grain, soft pigment blooms, granulation and small dry-brush marks show that it was painted by hand. No text, signature, watermark, border, frame or paper edge. No other birds, animals or people.
templates.scene: A hand-painted natural-history illustration in transparent watercolour with touches of gouache on warm cold-press paper, filling the picture edge to edge. The bird from <ref_image_0>, exactly as it appears there: the same pose and angle, the same feather pattern, colours and markings, the same bill, eye, legs and proportions, and the same sex and age (a dull female or young bird stays dull), nothing added and nothing taken away. Only the bird comes from <ref_image_0>, none of the branches, leaves, wires or background around it. It perches or stands naturally in the middle of the picture, large in the frame, about two fifths of its height, on a branch, post, lamp or the ground, whichever suits it and the place. Behind it is the place in <ref_image_1>, painted loosely in broad, soft-edged washes and dry-brush marks, simplified and slightly out of focus. The place keeps its own shapes and colours, under {edition_light}, with a few accents of {edition_colors}. The bird is painted in fine, confident detail with strokes that follow its feather tracts, crisp at the eye and bill, its colours true to <ref_image_0>; nothing covers its eye, bill or wing tips. {light} Visible paper grain, soft pigment blooms, granulation and small dry-brush marks show that it was painted by hand. No text, signature, watermark, border, frame or paper edge. No other birds, animals or people.
templates.photo: A hand-painted natural-history illustration in transparent watercolour with touches of gouache on warm cold-press paper, filling the picture edge to edge. The bird and the place from <ref_image_0>: the bird exactly as it appears there, in the same place in the frame, with the same pose and angle, the same feather pattern, colours and markings, the same bill, eye, legs and proportions, and the same sex and age (a dull female or young bird stays dull), nothing added and nothing taken away. Around it, the setting of <ref_image_0> is painted loosely in broad, soft-edged washes and dry-brush marks, simplified and slightly out of focus, keeping its own shapes and colours under {edition_light}. The bird is painted in fine, confident detail with strokes that follow its feather tracts, crisp at the eye and bill, its colours true to <ref_image_0>; nothing covers its eye, bill or wing tips. {light} Visible paper grain, soft pigment blooms, granulation and small dry-brush marks show that it was painted by hand. No text, signature, watermark, border, frame or paper edge. No other birds, animals or people.

isolate: A photograph of the bird from <ref_image_0>, exactly as it appears there: the same pose, angle, size and place in the frame, the same light, exposure and colour, and the same feathers, markings, eye, bill and feet, nothing added and nothing taken away. It stands out against a plain, even, pure white background. Everything that is not the bird is gone: branches, twigs, stems, wire, fence, leaves, flowers, perch, ground and background. Any part of the bird that was hidden behind them, such as its tail, a wing edge or its toes, is completed as it would look on this bird, in the same light. No shadow on the white.
